title: HELOC Statement

origin.title: Manulife One sample monthly statement (WM0013E)
origin.clearance_note: Manulife Bank's own sample statement, published in its advisor marketing materials and marked '(For illustrative purposes only)' and 'This is a sample statement only' on every page. The borrowers, mailing address and account number are placeholders ('Client name 1', 'Client address', 1234567) and the representative is a placeholder name. The site answers scripted requests with a 403, so the file used is the copy the document owner downloaded manually on 2026-04-04; its embedded title and form number (WM0013E, author Manulife Bank) match the url. No redaction was needed.

notes: Title is 'HELOC Statement', with HELOC capitalized, at the document owner's request. First built as the bank-statement sample; the document owner moved it here because Manulife One is not a standard bank statement but an all-in-one account secured on the borrower's home: a revolving home-equity line of credit (the $240,000 borrowing limit) combined with fixed- and variable-rate mortgage sub-accounts and everyday banking. The PDF's own metadata calls it a sample mortgage statement; for a US audience HELOC is the closer description, since it has no payment coupon or principal, interest and escrow split. The parse and extraction were not re-run for the move. The request named no page or fields. The page 1 snapshot was chosen because it tells one story, the month's movement on the account, and it reconciles: 155,268.51 + 3,967.76 out − 5,089.78 in = 154,146.49, a reduction of 1,122.02. This is an all-in-one mortgage account, so the running balance is borrowings and money in reduces it. The sample itself does not fully add up elsewhere: three of the 30 April rows in the main account's running balance differ from the arithmetic by a few dollars, and the four accounts' closing balances on pages 2 and 3 sum to 153,739.85, 406.64 less than the snapshot's 154,146.49. Extraction returns every figure as printed. statement_date and statement_period read OFF only because they are normalized (2023-05-01, 2023-04) from the printed 'Prepared on May 1, 2023' and 'Statement for April 2023'. account_holders includes the mailing panel's 'Client name' as well as the two borrowers.
